name: Limited contacts access
plain: The person lets the app see only chosen contacts, not the whole address book.
meaning: Shrinks contact exposure to a hand picked list; the app can also surface matching contacts inside its UI without a prompt.

android.permission: READ_CONTACTS still needed for broad reads; selection via picker
android.prompt_ui: Contact Picker sheet (Android 17) with field selection; legacy permission remains for full access
android.note: No persistent limited grant mode on Android; the picker returns a temporary Session URI

ios.prompt_ui: Allow Full Access, Limit Access (select contacts), Don't Allow
ios.note: ContactAccessButton shows contacts matching a search string and grants individual contacts with one tap; contactAccessPicker lets people revise the limited set

limits.headline: Can see only the contacts you choose on iPhone; Android gives only a one time pick
limits.user_action: You tap Limit Access and choose contacts, or pick from a list
can: Suggest matching contacts inside its own screen without a prompt (iPhone)
Add one more contact at a time when you tap it (iPhone)
Let you change the chosen set later (iPhone)
cannot: See contacts you did not select
Keep a limited grant on Android; the picker gives temporary access only
Open the whole address book without Allow Full Access
limits.differs: iPhone with iOS 18 and later has a lasting Limit Access mode; Android 17 has a picker with a temporary result and no lasting limited mode.

story.what_it_is: You let the app see only the contacts you pick, instead of the whole address book.

marketing.name: Limited Contacts Access
marketing.pitch: Share only selected contacts with an app. The app can ask to find matching people.

story.for_you: A sheet asks which contacts to share. You tick a few friends and the app only sees those. If you later search for someone else, the app can ask for just that person.
story.for_makers: Fewer people are afraid to say yes, and the app still gets what it needs. The system shows contacts that match what you type, and you can grant one at a time with a tap. The data is smaller and safer to keep.

use_cases.example: A chat app asks for the three people you want to invite, nothing more.
A split bill app lets you pick the friends to share a dinner with.
A game invite screen lets you pick teammates from your contacts.
A new photo app finds only the friends you choose.
A food app finds the person you want to send a gift to.
A kids' messaging app lets parents pick the approved contacts.
A safety app shares your location with only the picked contacts.

story.android_note: Android has no lasting limited mode. The picker returns a temporary access link for chosen contacts.
story.ios_note: iOS has a contact access button that shows matches and grants single contacts, plus a picker for lasting choice.

technical_bounds: Android has no standing partial grant, only a session picker
The limited set is stored per app
